coreIdea: Complete tree + parent≥children (max) or ≤ (min). NO left-right ordering (unlike BST). Root=extreme in O(1). Build-heap is O(n) bottom-up, NOT O(n log n).
mustRememberFormulas: Insert (bubble-up): O(log n). Delete/extract-root (sift-down): O(log n)
Build-heap bottom-up (from last internal node to root): O(n) total
Min-in-max-heap (or max-in-min-heap): Θ(n), must check all ⌈n/2⌉ leaves
Second-largest in max-heap: always a child of root (either one)
d-ary heap: height O(log_d n), but O(d) work per sift step

commonTrapsQuickList: Heap has NO left<right ordering — don't apply BST logic here
Build-heap is O(n), not O(n log n) — bottom-up sift-down from last internal node
Finding the opposite extreme (min-in-max-heap) is Θ(n), not O(log n)
Second-largest in max-heap is A child of root, not necessarily the left one
highYieldPyqLessons: Build-heap/heapify questions (5/30) and find-extreme questions (5/30) are the two most conceptually 'surprising' sub-patterns — most students get the complexity wrong on first exposure, so drill these specifically.
Always default to bottom-up sift-down for build-heap counting questions — top-down insertion gives a different (wrong) interchange count for these specific NAT questions.
